tasks.short: Search catalogues and databases for readings, read and select them, check library access and licences, format the bibliography, check the final list, and publish it to students.

steps.what: Business teacher searches catalogues and databases for specialized reading materials

loop.input: The course topics and level, and last year's reading list.
loop.output: A list of suggested readings with a line on each.
loop.check: Code keeps a suggestion only if it resolves by DOI or in the library catalogue; anything unresolved is dropped; the teacher selects.
loop.stop: One list per topic; topics with no resolving titles are flagged for a manual search.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword searches return hundreds of hits; suggesting what suits the course needs reading the abstracts.

steps.what: Business teacher reads and selects readings for outside reading assignments
Business teacher checks library access and licences for each reading
Business teacher compiles and formats the bibliography
Business teacher checks the final reading list
Business teacher uploads the reading list for students

tasks.design: A bounded step suggests readings per course topic; code keeps only titles that resolve by DOI or in the library catalogue, because invented references look real. The library's reading-list tool shows access and licence per item and links to the library's copy. A reference manager formats the list. Once the teacher has checked it, the list is published in the learning environment ({LMS}). Selecting what students read stays with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were searched by keyword, access checked one by one and lists typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Research tools suggest literature; library reading-list tools check access.
tasks.still_hard: The best reading for a course is one the teacher has read.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the one case study that makes students argue.
tasks.altitude: The teacher selects from checked suggestions instead of searching from scratch.

reach.learn: Whether licence problems are caught before the course starts.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and points to foundational papers.
A Leiden faculty memo notes that invented references pass plagiarism checks unflagged.

assumptions: Boundary: from course topics to the list published; buying new titles is outside.
Input contract: catalogue and licences from the library; fallback is manual searching.
Selecting readings stays with the teacher.
Students read the list as they do today.
research_questions: How many suggestions are dropped as unresolved?

already_counted.description: Business teacher reviews the suggested readings.

incremental.description: Business teacher reports broken library links.

approvals.approved_version: The reading list as checked by the teacher in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a short list of known readings; high: a new course with a long reading list.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Attend open days and graduations, give talks at community and alumni events, sign up for event duties, and prepare talks and stand material.

steps.what: Business teacher participates in campus events such as open days and graduations
Business teacher signs up for event duties by e-mail
Business teacher prepares the talk or stand material
Business teacher gives talks at community and alumni events

tasks.design: Event duties are signed up for in the faculty's event calendar ({CALENDAR}) instead of e-mail rounds. A current programme presentation and stand material kept by the marketing team sit in the document space ({DOCS}), so the teacher adapts them. Attending events and giving talks stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Duties were arranged by e-mail and each teacher built their own slides.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared event calendars and a central slide set are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Events fall on evenings and weekends that clash with other work.
tasks.human_edge: Convincing a doubtful parent that the programme suits their child.

reach.learn: Whether shared material keeps messages consistent.

evidence.claim: Shared event calendars can take duty sign-ups; document spaces hold a central slide set.

assumptions: Boundary: from the event calendar to the talk given; event organisation is outside.
Input contract: events planned by the faculty office; material kept by marketing; fallback is e-mail and own slides.
Attending and talking do not change.

incremental.description: Business teacher suggests updates to the central material.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few events a year; high: many open days and alumni events.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet the new colleague regularly, sit in on their classes and give feedback, answer practical questions, write the progress report for the teaching qualification, and send it to the coordinator.

steps.what: Business teacher mentors new faculty in regular meetings
Business teacher sits in on the new colleague's classes and gives feedback
Business teacher answers practical questions about systems and procedures by e-mail
Business teacher writes the progress report for the teaching qualification
Business teacher e-mails the progress report to the qualification coordinator

tasks.design: A faculty onboarding page ({DOCS}) answers the common practical questions on systems, rooms, exam rules and procedures, so the mentor answers fewer e-mails. The progress report for the teaching qualification is a form in the qualification portfolio system ({LMS}) with the colleague's courses filled in; once the mentor has completed it, it goes to the coordinator. Mentoring talks and class observation stay with the mentor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Practical questions came by e-mail and reports were paper forms filled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Onboarding pages and portfolio systems are common in universities.
tasks.still_hard: New colleagues often do not know what to ask.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a new colleague survive a lecture that went badly.

reach.learn: Whether the onboarding page cuts questions.

evidence.claim: Onboarding pages and portfolio systems can answer common questions and hold progress forms.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new colleague's start to the report submitted; the qualification assessment is outside.
Input contract: onboarding page kept by the faculty office; fallback is e-mail and paper forms.
Mentoring and observing do not change.
The new colleague's time does not change.
research_questions: Do practical questions to mentors fall?

incremental.description: Business teacher suggests missing answers for the onboarding page.

approvals.approved_version: The progress report as completed by the mentor in s4.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an experienced new colleague with few questions; high: a starter with many practical questions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Allocate teaching and research tasks, prepare and hold annual reviews, handle and decide budget and travel requests, pass approved requests to finance, and represent the department.

steps.what: Business teacher allocates teaching and research tasks as department head
Business teacher prepares the annual review forms for staff
Business teacher holds annual reviews with staff
Business teacher performs administrative duties such as handling budget and travel requests
Business teacher decides budget and travel requests
Business teacher forwards approved requests to finance
Business teacher represents the department in faculty meetings

tasks.design: A teaching-load planner adds up hours per staff member from the course catalogue and contracts, so overloads show before allocation. Annual review forms are prefilled with teaching load and publications from the research information system. Budget and travel requests come in through a workflow form ({WORKFLOW}) that shows the remaining budget; once the head decides, approved requests go to finance from the same form. Reviews with staff and faculty meetings stay with the head; prefilled data are a starting point, not a rating.
tasks.previous_blocker: Loads were added up in spreadsheets, review forms filled by hand and requests handled by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Load planners, research information systems and request workflows are common in universities.
tasks.still_hard: Fair allocation weighs history and wishes that no planner knows.
tasks.human_edge: Protecting a colleague's research time in a heavy teaching year.

evidence.claim: Teaching-load planners and request workflows with budget checks are common university tools.
Systems able to monitor staff need works council consent, for example per-staff dashboards.

assumptions: Boundary: from the course list to department represented; faculty budget setting is outside.
Input contract: course hours from the catalogue; publications from the research information system; fallback is spreadsheets and e-mail.
Reviews and decisions stay with the head.
Staff submit requests in the form in about the time an e-mail took.
research_questions: Do overloads get caught before the year starts?

incremental.description: Business teacher checks prefilled review data with staff.

approvals.approved_version: The requests as decided by the head in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small department; high: a large department with many requests.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The business teacher keeps choosing readings, representing the programme, mentoring and leading the department; searching titles, e-mail rounds and spreadsheet loads shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved time with colleagues and students.
